title: New development charges and Immigration Waterloo Region funding
subtitle: Also: Uptown sustainability vision, Moore Avenue reconstruction, Erb Street West commercial development, Microsoft agreement and Enova subordination.
overview: Council approved a new Development Charge By-law with rates taking effect April 1, 2026, and approved up to $2,394,000 in development charge debentures for the AMCC Sportsplex and McCormick Branch Library renovation and expansion {{vote:m8}}. A builders' group delegate argued that regional water capacity limits are stopping projects from getting permits, which could cause some to lose their frozen rates. Staff pointed to Section 27 agreements as a tool to address that later.

Council declined to give one-time transition funding to Immigration Waterloo Region. A motion for $25,000 from the Economic Development Reserve was defeated {{vote:m10}}, and council then chose the option of providing no funding {{vote:m11}}. Council also approved the Official Plan Amendment, rezoning and draft plan of subdivision for the Erb Street West commercial lands, which allow a new roundabout, a collector road and a new stormwater facility {{vote:m9}}.

Council awarded the Moore Avenue South reconstruction tender for $1,469,954.75 and endorsed the Sustainability Advisory Committee's Uptown vision. It also approved a three-year Microsoft agreement and an Enova Energy Corporation subordination agreement. Council met in closed session earlier in the day on drinking water infrastructure and a land transaction; the minutes report no public decisions from it.

decisions.detail: Council approved the new Development Charge By-law with new rates effective April 1, 2026, and up to $2,394,000 in debenture financing for the AMCC Sportsplex and library project.
Council approved Option 1, providing no one-time transition funding to Immigration Waterloo Region, after the $25,000 proposal was defeated.

Council approved the Official Plan Amendment, West Hill District Plan changes, rezoning and draft plan of subdivision for the Waterloo Commons lands and regional lands, with delegated approval authority to the Director of Planning.
Council awarded tender RFT26-07 to Regional Sewer and Watermain Ltd. for a total of $1,469,954.75.
Council accepted the Sustainability Advisory Committee report, asked the City to consider its recommendations and speed up actions, and set up regular progress updates on Uptown plans.
Council approved a new three-year agreement with Microsoft and CDW Canada and authorized the Mayor and Clerk to sign it.
Council approved the subordination agreement with the Bank of Montreal for the City's promissory notes with Enova and amended the delegation of authority schedule.

debate: A builders' group delegate said the rate increase, combined with the regional pause on development approvals over water capacity, could push projects past the 18-month rate-freeze window through no fault of their own. The delegate asked that affected projects keep their original rates. Staff said Section 27 agreements could extend the freeze for the City's portion of the charges, and the by-law already provides for them.

On development charges, one councillor asked why non-residential charges fall while residential charges rise. Staff said the rates reflect growth projections and added parks and recreation projects, which only residential development pays for.

On Immigration Waterloo Region, supporters cited avoiding job losses, the value of research and advocacy, and use of the Economic Development Reserve instead of the tax base. Opponents worried about opening the door to requests from other non-profits, backfilling federal funding cuts, and funding salaries of outside organizations.

On the Erb Street West lands, councillors asked about concerns raised by Six Nations, and staff said the tree compensation ratio was raised in response. Councillors also asked for pedestrian crossing safety at the new roundabout and traffic calming in the plaza. Staff confirmed final registration needs written regional confirmation of water capacity.

On the Uptown vision, a councillor said a planned 2026 Willis Way pedestrian pilot cannot go ahead because of a contractual obligation. The City is looking at short-term options with local businesses. Another councillor suggested a rubric for deciding when streets could be closed to cars.
